image_description: A close-up, side-profile photograph of an African crocodile's head and upper neck. The subject is facing left, with its mouth slightly open, revealing interlocking conical teeth. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing rough, bony scutes on the dorsal surface and smoother scales near the jawline. The eye is visible with a reptilian appearance. The background is a soft-focus blur of dry grass and earth tones.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers distinctly towards the nostrils, forming a V-shape characteristic of crocodiles rather than the U-shape of alligators. The profile matches the taxonomic description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows large, white, conical teeth. The fourth tooth on the lower jaw appears to fit into a notch in the upper jaw, confirming the 'interlocking' description even with the mouth slightly agape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned high on the skull (dorsal). While the pupil shape is hard to resolve perfectly at this resolution, the placement and general reptilian structure are correct. No obvious AI distortion in the eye region.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostril is clearly visible at the very end of the snout, consistent with the anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck are visible; the full body length cannot be verified from this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top of the head and neck show distinct, raised, bony ridges and textured scutes that align with the description of osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of greys and browns, and the texture is visibly rough and granular, matching the ground truth.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside (ventral surface) of the crocodile is not visible in this side-profile shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are completely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification (Nile crocodile vs. other crocodilians) based on snout shape and tooth arrangement.
To analyze the micro-texture of the scales for signs of AI smearing, repetition, or unnatural plasticity.
To ensure individual teeth are distinct entities and not fused with the gums or jawbone, a common AI failure mode.

focus_areas: Skin texture realism (scutes vs smooth scales)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the rough dorsal scutes and the smoother jaw scales. Verify if the teeth look like individual inserted objects or if they merge unnaturally with the gum line. Check for any 'melting' artifacts around the nostril and eye corners.
